description: The canonical bytes the system-domain Level-1 key signs over a holder authorization. CERTCRYPT uses TWO canonicalizations and this artifact takes the one that is NOT JCS: the bytes are insertion-ordered, in struct declaration order. Both digests are pinned below precisely so an implementation cannot pass by picking the wrong one and never finding out.

rules.canonicalization: Serialize the eight fields in THIS order — system_id, rules_version, system_root_fingerprint, authorized_role, authorization_issuer_kid, valid_from, valid_until, holder_key_set_root — as compact JSON: no spaces, no trailing newline, keys in insertion order (NOT sorted). That byte string is what gets signed.
rules.why_not_jcs: JCS sorts keys lexicographically, which reorders this object and yields a DIFFERENT digest — see expected_digest_if_jcs_wrongly_applied. An implementation that reaches for JCS here (the natural guess, since the evidence digest DOES use JCS) produces signatures that verify nowhere. Two canonicalizations coexist on purpose; this vector is the tripwire.
